## Intent
Hypothesis: a parallel-blend walk1 with a simple walk2 can approach the streaming bandwidth ceiling on this 68-byte-per-particle layout.

## Cache saturation
At q=0.01, ns/p falls from 9.538 (N=4000) to 6.147 (N=16000) — overhead amortization of the barrier and `___ulock_wait`/`___ulock_wake` coordination visible in the prologue. The curve is FLAT through the L2 spill at N≈61680: 5.943 at N=65000, 5.95 at N=262000, with only a slight rise to 6.203 at N=4M. No knee at L2→DRAM; the working set exceeds L2 but cost barely moves. The L1d spill at N≈963 is below the smallest measured point, already absorbed. Death rate raises the floor uniformly (q=0.05 ≈6.4, q=0.25 ≈8.5 ns/p) without changing the N-shape — additive per-particle respawn cost, not cache-mediated.

## Bandwidth
Peak is 11.44 GB/s at N=65000, q=0.01 — 45% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling. The plateau holds at ≈11 GB/s (q=0.01), ≈10.6 (q=0.05), ≈8.0 (q=0.25). Overhead-bound at small N (7.13 GB/s, N=4000), transitioning to a scatter-bound plateau by N=16000 that stays flat regardless of further N growth. It never approaches the ceiling; the gap is structural, not cache-mediated, since the plateau is identical from L2-resident through DRAM-resident sizes.

## Assembly
No vectorization — zero vector-suffixed instructions in 245 total. All FP work is scalar: `fmul`, `fadd`, `fsub`, `fcvtzs` on single registers (`s0`–`s17`). Particle components load via scalar `ldp s5, s6` and `ldr s17`. The neighbor scatter is byte-granular: `ldrb w2, [x1]`, `add w2, w2, w12`, `cmp w2, #0xff`, `csel`, `strb w2, [x1]` — repeated three times per neighbor for RGB, plus `strb w11` for the self-write. No gather. The per-byte read-modify-write with saturation clamp serializes dependent loads and stores that cannot coalesce into wider transactions, capping bandwidth at 45% of ceiling.

## Verdict
Refuted — peak 11.44 GB/s is 45% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling, with 0 vector instructions and byte-granular `strb`/`ldrb` scatter that cannot stream. The plateau is flat from N=16000 through N=4M (6.1–6.2 ns/p at q=0.01), confirming the bottleneck is scalar codegen, not cache capacity. Death rate only raises the floor to 8.5 ns/p at q=0.25 without changing the N-shape.
